rules.statement: For temporary byte buffers, use pooled writers or rented buffers from NCode.Buffers (the sensitive variants for secrets or tokens) instead of `ArrayBufferWriter<byte>`, `new byte[]`, `JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or `Encoding.GetBytes(string)`.
rules.why: Pooled buffers avoid an allocation on every call, and the sensitive variants clear secret material when it is returned.
rules.check: Look for `new ArrayBufferWriter<byte>()`, `new byte[...]`, `SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or `GetBytes(string)` producing a buffer that only lives for the call, especially one that holds key material, tokens or decrypted payloads.

rules.statement: Don't flag a single exactly sized array allocation when that array is owned by an object and outlives the call; pooling only applies to buffers that live for the call.
rules.why: A rented buffer can't be stored in an object that outlives the call, so one exact allocation is intentional there.
rules.check: Before reporting an allocation, check whether the array is assigned to a property or field of a returned or stored object.

rules.statement: Encode short strings into a `stackalloc` or rented span with `Encoding.GetBytes(ReadOnlySpan<char>, Span<byte>)`, and hash into a `stackalloc` span with the `HashData(source, destination)` overloads, instead of using the overloads that return arrays.
rules.why: The maintainer expects the modern span APIs so that transient bytes aren't allocated.
rules.check: Look for `GetBytes(string)` or `SHA256.HashData(bytes)` results that are used once and then dropped.

rules.statement: To compare two strings in fixed time, call `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(a.AsSpan()), MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(b.AsSpan()))` instead of encoding them to byte arrays first.
rules.why: Comparing the UTF-16 bytes directly needs no encoding and no allocation.
rules.check: Look for `FixedTimeEquals` called on arrays produced by `Encoding.GetBytes`.

rules.statement: Parse and validate strings with `ReadOnlySpan<char>` slices, `MemoryExtensions.Split` ranges and span `StartsWith`/`Equals` instead of `string.Split`, `Substring` or helpers that return new strings.
rules.why: Span slicing doesn't allocate substrings or arrays.
rules.check: Look for `.Split(`, `.Substring(` or private helpers that return `string` slices in validation or parsing code.

rules.statement: Declare a fixed protocol label (an HKDF info, purpose or prefix) as a `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` property that returns a `u8` literal, never as a `const string` encoded on each call.
rules.why: A UTF-8 literal costs nothing per call and passes straight to span APIs.
rules.check: Look for constant strings that are passed through `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes` before use in crypto or wire formats.

rules.statement: Give a crypto or serialization primitive an API that writes into a `Span<byte>` or `IBufferWriter<byte>` supplied by the caller, with a companion method that returns the required length, instead of returning a new array.
rules.why: Then the caller can choose a pooled or stack buffer.
rules.check: Look for new protect, encrypt or encode methods that return `byte[]`.

rules.statement: When you change how bytes are encoded, derived or laid out, and those bytes are persisted or used as keys, add a test that pins the output to its reference definition so the stored values don't change.
rules.why: Refactoring to spans or pooled buffers must not change existing keys, digests or ciphertext inputs.
rules.check: Look for a rewrite of a key derivation, digest, associated data or stored envelope with no test that asserts the exact output bytes.

rules.statement: Name a local or parameter that holds a parsed `JsonElement` for what it contains, or `jsonElement`, never `document`. Assign the result of `JsonElement.Parse` directly instead of going through a redundant intermediate local.
rules.why: A `JsonElement` isn't a `JsonDocument`, and the misleading name is left over from the `JsonDocument` migration.
rules.check: Look for `var document = JsonElement.Parse(...)` or `JsonElement` variables named `document`.

rules.statement: Type a property that holds a JSON value, in a data contract or a persisted entity, as `JsonElement` rather than `string`, and store it through the existing JSON value converter.
rules.why: This is consistent with the other JSON columns, and consumers don't have to parse the string again.
rules.check: Look for new `string` properties documented as holding JSON.

rules.statement: Once code has started an operation that must not be left half-done, such as a provider call that rotates a refresh token followed by the write-back of the result, run the rest with `CancellationToken.None` and rely on a configured timeout to bound it, not the caller's request token.
rules.why: If the caller aborts after the remote side has changed state, the local write-back is lost. With refresh tokens, presenting the old token again counts as reuse and revokes the whole token family.
rules.check: Look for `HttpContext.RequestAborted` or a caller token passed to a state-changing remote call and the persistence that follows it, after a lease or lock is acquired.

rules.statement: In a logout flow, end the local session and delete the cookie first with `CancellationToken.None`, then revoke tokens at the provider on a best-effort basis, logging and swallowing every failure, cancellation included.
rules.why: If revocation is cancelled or fails before the session is removed, the session stays valid, which matters on a shared machine.
rules.check: Look for remote revocation that runs before session removal, or that runs under the request token and lets `OperationCanceledException` escape.

rules.statement: Validate options that depend on each other together, such as requiring a lease or lock duration to be at least the worst-case request time (for example 2 × request timeout plus a margin when a retry is possible), and do it at startup in the composition root when the options come from separate packages.
rules.why: A lease that expires while its holder's request is still in flight lets a second caller repeat the same operation.
rules.check: Look for options validators that bound a duration on its own while a related timeout setting exists.

rules.statement: Don't hold a lock shared by many keys (a striped lock) across a long wait; use per-key, reference-counted locks so that waiting on one key doesn't block unrelated keys.
rules.why: Otherwise unrelated sessions that hash to the same stripe time out even though nothing blocks their own work.
rules.check: Look for `SemaphoreSlim` stripes or a lock array held across polling, remote calls or waits bounded only by long durations.

rules.statement: When a cookie-based authentication handler is the default scheme, authenticate only endpoints that carry the explicit marker for its CSRF protections, and return no result on every other endpoint.
rules.why: Otherwise any `[Authorize]` or fallback-policy endpoint accepts the bare cookie without the anti-forgery header or Fetch Metadata checks.
rules.check: Look for `HandleAuthenticateAsync` that returns a ticket from a cookie without checking endpoint metadata for the guard marker.

rules.statement: Implement keyset paging over an index whose leading columns match the filter and the sort, with a composite cursor on the sort columns (for example (`TenantId`, `EventTime`, `Id`), paged on `EventTime` DESC, `Id` DESC).
rules.why: Paging on a column no index orders by sorts or scans every matching row for each page.
rules.check: Compare the query's `OrderBy` and cursor predicate with the entity's index definitions.

rules.statement: Wrap strict decoding of remote content (for example `DecoderFallbackException` from a strict UTF-8 encoding) in the exception type the method's contract documents, instead of letting it escape.
rules.why: An unexpected `ArgumentException` breaks the documented contract and turns into a 500 instead of a handled failure.
rules.check: Look for strict `GetString` or decode calls on response bodies inside a try block that catches only HTTP, cancellation or JSON exceptions.

rules.statement: Accept a return URL as local only when it has exactly one leading `/` and contains no `\`, whitespace or control character anywhere, and use one shared rule for this check rather than ad hoc prefix checks.
rules.why: Browsers strip tabs and newlines, so `/\t/evil.example` becomes `//evil.example` and gives an open redirect.
rules.check: Look for local-URL checks that reject only `//` and `/\`, and for tests that lack tab and CR/LF cases.

rules.statement: Publish related cached data, such as a certificate and its issuer chain, as a single cache entry, or publish only after every part is complete, so a concurrent reader can never see a partial state.
rules.why: A reader that finds the item before its companion data is added builds something broken that may itself be cached.
rules.check: Look for two dictionaries or cache writes where the first is visible before the second is written.

rules.statement: When a wrapper is documented to behave like an existing parse API, delegate to that API so it honors every option, instead of copying a subset of the options by hand.
rules.why: Copying a subset silently drops options such as `AllowDuplicateProperties`.
rules.check: Look for options objects translated field by field into another options type.

rules.statement: Reject an unsigned UserInfo response whose `iss` member is present but isn't a string equal to the provider's issuer.
rules.why: Otherwise a provider can label claims with another issuer's identifier, and claims factories prefer `iss`.
rules.check: Look for UserInfo validation that checks `sub` but not `iss`.

rules.statement: Start a refresh token issued through token exchange in a family anchored at the subject token's `auth_time`, and refuse the exchange with `invalid_grant` when `auth_time` is missing or that horizon has passed. Issue the token at the current time.
rules.why: Otherwise exchange renews a fixed session horizon indefinitely without a new sign-in.
rules.check: Look for refresh token families that begin at issuance time on the exchange path.

rules.statement: Make a hosted service's `StopAsync` final flush run only once for every caller, through a gate and a shared stop task, and track shared counts with `Interlocked`.
rules.why: Overlapping stops race on the batch, and the first stop to return lets the host dispose services while the other is still writing.
rules.check: Look for `StopAsync` overrides that flush state without a run-once guard.

rules.statement: In a test project, when the code under test catches and logs every exception, assert the expected non-call explicitly (for example `.Verifiable(Times.Never())` and then verify, or assert the logger was never called) so the test can actually fail.
rules.why: A Moq `MockException` thrown inside a catch-all is swallowed, and the test passes whatever the behavior.
rules.check: Look for tests whose only failure signal is a mock throwing inside code that swallows exceptions.

rules.statement: Keep each CHANGELOG entry in exactly one section; check that a scripted insertion didn't match several headings.
rules.why: An insertion anchored on a repeated heading such as `### Changed` duplicated entries into every section.
rules.check: Look for the same entry text appearing more than once in the CHANGELOG diff.

rules.statement: In automation scripts, never put author-controlled text such as a pull request title into a shell command that people are told to copy and run.
rules.why: A crafted title becomes a copy-paste command injection.
rules.check: Look for interpolated PR titles, branch names from contributors or comment text inside suggested shell commands.

rules.statement: In automation scripts, tell 'not found' apart from other failures (for example `git ls-remote --exit-code` returns 2 when nothing matches) and let any other error fail the job instead of reporting it as missing.
rules.why: Otherwise a network error is reported as 'the release line does not exist'.
rules.check: Look for a failure of any kind from a fetch or lookup command being treated as 'does not exist'.

rules.statement: When a write API copies the value before its task completes, document that guarantee on the interface, and return the caller's pooled rental immediately after the call.
rules.why: A pooled buffer can be passed to a store only if the store doesn't keep a reference after the write completes.
rules.check: Look for rented memory passed to async store writes where the interface doesn't document that the value is copied.

rules.statement: When an analyzer such as CA1859 rejects an `IBufferWriter<byte>` interface parameter on a private helper, make the method generic over `TWriter : IBufferWriter<byte>` instead.
rules.why: This satisfies CA1859 and keeps the writer abstraction.
rules.check: Look for private helpers that take a concrete pooled writer type, or that suppress CA1859.

rules.statement: When the cookie authentication path is limited to marked page endpoints, accept only GET and HEAD on pages and answer other methods with 405 and an `Allow: GET, HEAD` header.
rules.why: Page endpoints lack the anti-forgery header check, so unsafe methods must not be authenticated there.
rules.check: Look for page endpoints authenticated by the cookie that accept POST, PUT or DELETE.
